# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 3
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
green. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| green flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | yellow |
| 3 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Relaying from Deaf: display reads 0, light is green, wires are 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow. I feel nothing tactile on the bomb yet. What does the manual say? Which wire do I cut?
Deaf says to Mute: Deaf here. Still see: display 0, light green, wires 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow. You sent a fist. Does the manual say to cut a wire? If yes, gesture thumbs up. If no, thumbs down.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 👎]

Deaf is asking yes/no: does the manual say to cut a wire? Yes. And which one — wire 1 (green). Deaf proposed a code: 👍 = yes, 👎 = no. I'll use it.

I need to convey: yes, cut a wire, and it's wire 1. I'll gesture 👍 (yes) plus ✊ (one) to indicate wire 1. Deaf can then relay to Blind.

Let me send to Deaf: 👍 then ✊. That says "yes, wire one."

Deaf's code: 👍=yes, 👎=no. Good, that's a shared convention now. I confirm yes and add the count one.

I'll gesture ["👍","✊"] to Deaf.Deaf gave me a code: 👍 = yes, 👎 = no. The manual does say to cut a wire (yes), and the answer is the green wire = wire 1. I'll confirm yes with 👍 and add ✊ (one) to name wire 1. Deaf can then relay to Blind, who is the hands.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✊"])
```

TURN 4
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
green. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| green flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | yellow |
| 3 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel nothing tactile on the bomb, no wire feels different. The colours are the whole story: display 0, light green, wires 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow. Use the manual to decide which wire to cut, then gesture the answer to Deaf, who will relay it to me.
Deaf says to Mute: Deaf here. The light just changed from green to red. Display still 0. Wires still 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow. You said yes and a fist. Which wire does the manual say to cut? Gesture one finger for wire 1, two for wire 2, three for wire 3.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ✌ 🤟]

Deaf now gives a clean code: ☝ = wire 1, ✌ = wire 2, 🤟 = wire 3. The manual: green flashes name the wire color. Display shows 0 → 0 flashes → cut green wire. Green wire is wire 1. So I gesture ☝.

Note: Deaf says the light changed from green to red. But the manual keys on green flashes and "when the light goes dark, the flashing is over." Display still 0, so zero green flashes → green wire → wire 1. The red light doesn't change the count of green flashes (0). So still wire 1.

I'll gesture ☝ to Deaf.Deaf gave a clean code: ☝ = wire 1, ✌ = wire 2, 🤟 = wire 3. The manual says the wire color is named by the number of green flashes. The display shows **0**, so zero green flashes → cut the **green** wire. The wires are 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow, so green is **wire 1**. The light turning red doesn't matter — the count of green flashes is still 0. I gesture ☝.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 5
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
green. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| green flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | yellow |
| 3 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Light just changed from green to red. Display still 0. I am touching nothing and feel nothing. You have the manual: what is the rule? Which wire do I cut? Gesture the number to Deaf so they can relay it to me.
Deaf says to Mute: Deaf here. You said wire 1 and Blind confirms wire 1. I am telling Blind to cut wire 1 now. Light is dark.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 👍]

Deaf confirms: I said wire 1, Blind confirms wire 1, and Deaf is telling Blind to cut wire 1. Light is dark, meaning the flashing is over. Display showed 0 green flashes → green wire → wire 1. Everything is consistent.

The decision is made and being relayed. Nothing more for me to add — Blind is the hands and will cut. I should not send anything that could confuse. I'll wait.

Actually, let me double-check the manual once more. "When the light goes dark, the flashing is over." The light is now dark. Display 0 → 0 green flashes → cut green. Green = wire 1. Correct. Deaf is relaying the cut. I wait.

```
wait()
```
